critical_code_review_comments: studio_sensitivity.score_sensitivity: the M&A-only case (no HR/litigation triggers) lands at 45 (internal band), not confidential — this is the iter63 spec saying 'higher than benign' and is intentional by the rule weights, but the user may expect pure M&A to auto-tag confidential. Flag for product review: consider bumping M&A weight from 20 → 30 OR lowering confidential band threshold from 50 → 45 if 'M&A alone = confidential' is the desired policy. Verified restricted trigger path still hits 75+ correctly.
studio.py record_view uses find_one_and_update upsert with compound unique index — race-safe, identical pattern to iter63 _consume_free_grant. Good.
studio.py /engagement .to_list(length=500) caps views at 500 per artefact — fine today, flag if a deck starts accruing >500 views (unlikely for board artefacts).
studio_history aggregates views/shares in one pipeline per collection — efficient. Sort key uses string-compare on ISO timestamps — works because all created_at are same tz and format.

briefings.py line 143-148 and decks.py line 360-367 both try/except the sensitivity scoring — on failure they set sensitivity=None. Good defensive coding but it silently swallows real bugs; consider a single-line logger.warning in the except branch for observability.
server.py index on (artefact_kind, artefact_id, account_id, day_utc) unique — exactly right for the dedup contract.
